text:
alex: Heads up — apiserver 503s in us-west2 starting ~11:02 UTC. Seems tied to a bursty GPU attach wave from an onboarding job. Saw etcd leader re-election and controller-manager restarted twice. Dropping traces here.

sre-bot: incident created INC-20260322-11:05 (severity: high) :rotating_light:

Dina: Can you paste the apiserver + etcd excerpts? Also which GPU pool?

alex: Pool: gpu-pool-usw2-fast. Minimal excerpts:
```
I0322 11:02:07.123 apiserver request failed: context deadline exceeded (GET /api/v1/watch/namespaces)
E0322 11:02:09.456 etcdserver: leader changed, term=42, took 1.8s
E0322 11:02:10.789 controller-manager: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address (recovered)
```

kevin: NVMe iops and io_latency graphs spiking at the same time. see dashboard: http://grafana/boards/usw2-nvme (shortlink)

olivia: Looks like attach wave triggered massive WAL/flushing on etcd peers (nvme pressure) which then pushed apiserver watch cache to timeout -> reconnections -> controller-manager backlog. Two suggested mitigations: 1) throttle attach rate on provisioner (token-bucket) 2) temporary reduce apiserver watch retention to shrink memory pressure.

alex: Can we throttle quickly? Where is the provisioner config?

olivia: It's in the cluster-config cm: `gpu-provisioner` (namespace infra). Quick patch we can apply:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch cm gpu-provisioner -p '{"data":{"max_attach_per_sec":"4","burst":"8"}}' || true
# then restart provisioner pod: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/gpu-provisioner
```
This will limit attach throughput and smooth NVMe IO.

kevin: Agree. Also bump etcd election timeout by 50% for the short window? Risky but reduces leader churn. Example patch for kube-apiserver flags, we can increment `--etcd-servers-timeout` and `--request-timeout` for a canary.

Dina: I'll prepare the patch for the provisioner and a controlled restart. Olivia, can you coordinate a quick canary in a single AZ?

olivia: On it. Rolling to az-a1 first. Will keep rollback ready.

alex: I'm going to throttle onboarding jobs at the source too (rate-limit the orchestrator). Also reducing new node attachments by 60% for 10m.

sre-bot: change applied: gpu-provisioner cm patched by olivia at 11:09. rollout restart started (deploy/gpu-provisioner)

kevin: NVMe p95 latency trending down after patch. apiserver 5xx rate dropping from 12% -> 1.8% in last 6m.

alex: Nice. Keep monitoring. Next steps: (1) add token-bucket to provisioner code for long-term (olivia/infra-plat) (2) add pre-attach rate limiting by customer onboarding pipeline (product/eng) (3) run a postmortem once stable and calculate cost impact of slowed attach vs risk.

Dina: Adding action items to INC-20260322 and assigning owners.

sre-bot: Incident severity lowered to medium at 11:18. apiserver error rate: 0.9% (still above baseline).

alex: Thanks all — keeping this thread for notes. If error rate hits baseline for 30m we'll close.

olivia: I'll open a PR for token-bucket + config knobs (ETA 1 business day).

sre-bot: update: 11:32 — apiserver 5xx at baseline. Marking resolved pending postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
